target_customer: Foreign tourists and NRIs visiting India who want to pay by UPI
problem: Visitors to India relied on ATMs and costly foreign exchange. Cheq let them load a UPI wallet with international cards and pay at merchants.
business_model: Consumer wallet earning forex and payment fees
product_category: Fintech UPI wallet for inbound travellers

competitors.name: NPCI UPI One World
competitors.what: Prepaid UPI wallet for foreign visitors, first for G20 country travellers
competitors.funding_then: not applicable, run by the payments network

technical_complexity.rationale: A UPI wallet needs KYC for foreigners, a bank or PPI licence partner and merchant payments integration, with partner and regulatory work more than novel engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The RBI opened UPI to visitors in February 2023 and NPCI offered its own wallet, so the wedge was open to banks and payments networks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: NPCI extended UPI One World to all inbound travellers in July 2024 and Bank of Baroda launched UPI Global QR for visitors.

market_need_then: RBI allowed foreign nationals and NRIs to use UPI in February 2023 and tourists faced ATMs and forex fees, with inbound travel recovering after the pandemic.

branding.domain_note: Company site chequpi.com and cheq.money in use; exact domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain pitch about avoiding ATMs and forex costs

brand_strength.rationale: Indian business press covered the YC raise, but no source discusses the brand itself. The Cheq spelling is easy to misread, and other firms named CheQ and Cheq exist.

outcome_analysis: Cheq launched in 2021 and joined YC in Summer 2023 after RBI opened UPI to visitors, and raised about $500,000 from Y Combinator. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquisition report was found and the app store listing still shows an operating wallet, so the exit is unverified. NPCI and banks moved into the same inbound traveller wedge in 2023 and 2024, which pressured a standalone wallet.
notes: Exit type is unknown and conflicts with the directory status Acquired; the outcome search found no acquisition. cheq.money did not resolve in this session so the site status is unverified. YC amount of $500K reported by several outlets; some call it seed. Aggregator totals of $10.5M to $10.81M (Inc42, others) are unverified and look inflated. CB Insights names Aditya Soni as founder of a Cheq entry, likely a different company. Operator reported as Terrafin Solutions with a Transcorp PPI arrangement; RBI reportedly moved against co-branded PPIs on UPI (Entrackr).
